group: block list with halving counts (exp/sqrt), not solved
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Up to renaming, the machine is the table of a DeepMind proof (busycoq pull request 93) with its halting transition replaced. A Coq proof built from that file needs only one more thing, a stop of its accelerated engine, and the engine has not stopped in more than 107765 steps. The place where the sibling halts recurs in this run once per lap, and this machine gets past it the same way every time; nothing in the run comes near the one pattern that could halt it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,697 cells have been visited and 23,608 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.115). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).

claims.title: 10 sweep rules, for all n
claims.text: The head crosses a run of n copies of a short word (10, 110, 100, 011, ...) in one go, for all n and any tape around it; for example L (110)n 1 1 B> 0 R becomes L B> 1 1 (100)n 1 R in 5n + 2 steps.

claims.title: Rounds and block lists
claims.text: A C run of 109 steps reaches the left end in state E 29 times (counting only events at least 106 steps apart). Each time the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00; almost all blocks have length 6m + 1 and stand in runs of equal blocks, longest blocks on the left.

claims.title: Counts halve each round
claims.text: From one round end to the next, the number of blocks of length 6m + 1 becomes about half (within a few blocks) the number of blocks of length 6(m − 1) + 1 before; a new run of blocks 1 appears on the right, alternately about 2,000 to 4,000 and about 200 to 450 long in the last rounds. A few irregular blocks sit at the boundaries of the runs.

claims.title: A marker sweeping left
claims.text: Between round ends the head goes back and forth across most of the tape; the point where it turns moves left a few cells per trip while each trip adds a few cells on the right. This is why the right side grows like the square root of the step count and the left side, which only grows at round ends, like its logarithm.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.33×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 2.33×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 6,537 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: A halt needs B reading 0 with 0, 0, 1 on its left
claims.text: E is entered only by D0, D by B1 (which leaves a 0 behind it) or C0, and C only by B0, so the last four steps of a halting run start in state B reading 0 with the cells 0, 0, 1 to its left, nearest first: an internal run of exactly three 0s entered from its right end.

claims.title: A Coq proof that only needs the engine to stop
claims.text: coq/mkU.py rewrites the DeepMind proof of busycoq pull request 93 for this machine. Up to swapping E and F the machine is that proof's table with F merged into E (so the sibling's halting transition becomes a step) and with D0 replaced by a three-step detour that halts exactly when D reads 0 with a 1 on its left. The file compiles with Coq 8.20.1 and Print Assumptions lists only run_ok, the statement that the engine stops; with it the file would prove that the machine halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7765</sup> steps
claims.text: The engine of that proof file, extracted to OCaml with Coq's binary numbers realized by Zarith (the same engine as for starts B and D of the table, whose full compressed states equal those of the plain extraction at fast steps 35,227,304 and 29,077,778 of those runs; the plain extraction was checked against direct simulation through 3×10<sup>9</sup> steps), ran 601,531,739 fast steps from blank tape without stopping (22 November 2026). Its tape then has more than 2<sup>25798</sup> cells, each visited at least once. Every entry into raw mode (where a halt would have to happen; the engine checks each raw step for one) falls into the same few classes as in the earlier runs: D moving right with a 0 on its left, D moving left onto a 1, B moving right, or the sibling’s halting event (C reading 0 with 1 1 1 on its left), which this machine survives each time.
claims.where: coq/README.md, runz.ml in the start-A folder of the table

claims.title: The sibling's halting point recurs and is survived
claims.text: A halt can only happen where the engine leaves its macro rules. Through 18.4 million fast steps it left them only in 14 kinds of local situation, all at the left end of the written tape. One of them, C reading 0 with 1 1 1 on its left, is exactly where the sibling of pull request 93 halts; here it recurred 10 times, with the same nearest cells each time, and each time the machine erased three 1s and went back to the macro rules. No exit met the cells 0, 1 that a halt needs. So the sibling's halting point predicts no halting point for this machine, and a halt would need a kind of exit the run has never produced.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The Coq file above would settle it if the engine ever stopped; a proof that it never halts would need the closed form of the DeepMind counter's laps, including that no lap ever ends in the three-0 pattern.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine writes a list of blocks of 1s and, round after round, merges them: every round there are about half as many blocks of each size, each six cells longer, and a fresh supply of short blocks is fed in on the right. This page runs the real machine, shows the lists, and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt: the accelerated engine of the Coq proof file has not stopped in 601,531,739 of its steps.
The Coq proof of halting is complete except for the engine run, which has not stopped.
Sweep rules proved in Lean for all n.
The count of each block size halves from one round to the next (simulation).
No halt in the C simulator.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: A list of blocks
html: Each time the head reaches the left end of the tape in state E, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00. Almost every block has length 6m + 1 (1, 7, 13, 19, …), and equal blocks stand together: on the right a long run of blocks 1, then a run of blocks 17, then 113, and so on, the longest on the left. A handful of irregular blocks sit between the runs.

sections.heading: Halve and move up
html: Read down a diagonal of the table: the count of blocks of length 6m + 1 in one row is about half (within a few blocks) the count of blocks of length 6(m − 1) + 1 in the row before. So each round pairs up the blocks of every run and turns each pair into one block six cells longer, while a new run of blocks 1 is added on the right, alternately long and short. In this sense the tape holds numbers written in a base-2 like system, one run per digit position.

The rounds are made of sweeps the head does in one go; Lean proves 10 of them for all lengths (lean/Rules.lean). Inside a round the head goes back and forth across most of the tape, turning at a point that moves left a few cells per trip, and each trip adds a few cells on the right. That is why the right side of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, and the left side, which grows only at round ends, like its logarithm.

sections.heading: How it would halt
html: The only halting transition is E1. State E is entered by D0 (write 1, move left), so the machine halts exactly when one of these moves lands on a 1. At the left end the head enters E on blank tape and goes on; inside the block list the irregular blocks at the run boundaries are where such a landing could happen. Nothing seen so far does it, and no invariant that rules it out is known.

To decide the machine one would need the round map in closed form, including what the odd counts and the irregular blocks at the run boundaries do, and then an argument about where E can land. The halving pattern suggests a counter-like invariant may exist; none has been found.

20 November 2026. Up to swapping E and F this machine is the table of a DeepMind halting proof (busycoq pull request 93) with two changes: the sibling's halting transition becomes a step that keeps erasing to the left, and D0 becomes a detour that halts exactly when D reads 0 with a 1 on its left. Lean proves that a halt needs state B reading 0 with 0, 0, 1 to its left (lean/Halt.lean). The sibling's accelerated engine, rebuilt for this machine, has run past 107765 steps without stopping. The configuration where the sibling halts recurs once per lap of its counter (111 times through 6.0·108 fast steps), always with the same nearest cells, and each time this machine erases three 1s and carries on. No situation that could lead to a halt has appeared (coq/README.md).

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

summary: DeepMind pull request 93's table with its halt removed and a detour halt added; the Coq proof waits only for an engine stop, none in 10^7765 steps; the sibling's halting point recurs and is survived each lap. Open.
